Tier 2: modify model_design and training_evaluation by adding a learned relative recency bias to the existing recurrent attention. The independent candidate embedding experiment reduced macro HR@10 to 0.5350, so retain the supplied model’s shared history/candidate embedding. The current attention retrieves earlier recurrent states by content but has no explicit representation of their distance from the prediction position. A possible limitation is that similar historical states receive comparable attention despite different relevance as interests change; the available results do not establish this as the cause of the plateau.

Add one jointly trained relative-position bias table to the attention logits before causal masking and softmax. For query position t and earlier position s, index the table using a logarithmic bucket of t−s, distinguishing nearby events precisely while grouping distant events. Initialize all biases to zero so the initial attention behavior matches the supplied architecture, and preserve the GRU, shared embeddings, projection, scoring function, sampled-softmax objective, optimizer, sampling, and hyperparameters. This isolates whether learning distance preferences improves retrieval without introducing another predictor or independently fitted scores.

Update the predictor writer to reconstruct this architecture and strictly load exactly one newly trained checkpoint per category, including the bias table. Extend the existing gradient, causality, and checkpoint checks to cover the new parameter, while retaining identical validation and inference preprocessing, all four routes, supplied splits, seeds, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Select checkpoints using the existing fixed validation protocol and assess the change through pinned-host macro HR@10 against 0.5713 and the best reported 0.5737, without accessing hidden test data.
